items.title: Africa: 22 African Countries Face Debt Distress, 14 At High Risk - AfDB

original_payload.original_title: Africa: 22 African Countries Face Debt Distress, 14 At High Risk - AfDB
original_payload.original_body:
The African Development Bank (AfDB) has disclosed that 14 African countries were at high risk of debt distress as of July 2026, while eight others were already in debt distress, highlighting the growing pressure of public borrowing on the continent's economies.
The bank warned that rising debt-service obligations were increasingly constraining governments' fiscal space, limiting their capacity to fund essential services and development priorities.
The disclosure was contained in AfDB's November 2026 report, Africa's Macroeconomic Performance and Outlook, which examined the continent's public debt situation and growing vulnerabilities.
According to the report, the growing reliance of African governments on external commercial and domestic borrowing has driven up debt-service costs and heightened vulnerabilities.

items.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - November 20, 2026

original_payload.original_title: Africa: All of Africa Today - November 20, 2026
original_payload.original_body:
Dozens Missing After Migrant Boat Capsizes Off Senegal
Search operations are continuing off Senegal's Atlantic coast after a boat carrying an estimated 50 to 100 migrants  capsized  near Yenne, south of Dakar. Four bodies have been recovered, while dozens remain missing. The latest tragedy comes less than two weeks after another shipwreck killed at least 39 people. Senegalese President Diomaye Faye has called for an investigation into the factors driving irregular migration. The International Organisation for Migration estimates that at least 454 people have died or gone missing along the West African coast this year. Survivors told authorities that the boat was carrying about 100 people, including five women. The Senegalese navy also reported rescuing more than 1,400 people during operations on Monday and Tuesday, highlighting the scale of irregular migration along the Atlantic route.

items.title: Somalia: UAE Condemns What It Calls Somalia's Escalating Hostile Conduct

original_payload.original_title: Somalia: UAE Condemns What It Calls Somalia's Escalating Hostile Conduct
original_payload.original_body:
Abu Dhabi — The United Arab Emirates has strongly condemned what it described as increasingly hostile conduct by the Somali government, saying recent actions threaten diplomatic relations and cooperation between the two countries.
In a statement, the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs said decisions affecting bilateral relations should be guided by shared interests and kept separate from political considerations and domestic disputes.
The ministry also expressed concern over what it described as Somalia's attempt to bring internal disagreements over power-sharing into relations between the two countries, warning that such developments could negatively affect the interests of their two brotherly peoples.
